newsitem.title: USA: House's Armey says tobacco deal needs "long" study.
newsitem.headline: House's Armey says tobacco deal needs "long" study.

text.p: U.S. House Majority Leader Dick Armey said Tuesday the proposed tobacco settlement would have "to be studied for a long time."
"It'll take some time," Armey told reporters. "Whether it's next year or not, I don't know the answer."

Armey, a Texas Republican, said he had not yet read the proposed $368 billion settlement between the tobacco industry and the 40 states suing it, and had no initial reaction as to where he would like Congress to make changes in the proposal.
"I'd have to have a staff of experts around," he said, adding that at least three House committees would be involved in any effort to pass legislation to enact the agreement.

Armey said he did not expect the House this week to consider a proposal, contained in the Senate Finance Committee's tax bill, to raise cigarette taxes by 20 cents to pay for children's health insurance. That proposal is not part of the House tax cut bill, set for a vote Thursday.

He said he does not favor higher cigarette taxes, because he does not like any tax increases. But asked whether he would definitely rule out cigarette tax hikes, he said, "Anything that is properly packaged for the right reasons with the correct labels on it, is probably something I'd be willing to look at, but I have no predilection in favor of raising that tax any more than I would have of raising any other taxes.
